principles: Gate rules must be mechanically enforceable, not prompt-only.
Escalation should target risky stories without making ordinary clean stories pay the full review cost.
Host independence must be proven from durable identity, session, and key facts rather than display strings.
Decision-doc policy changes remain high-impact and always require 3x2.
drivers: The user requested all development to automatically follow 3x2 when first REVIEW round finds two or more problems.
The B-2c0c audit found the existing decision-doc quorum independence proof is too weak.
Open-source contributors need a clear execution document before code changes.

options.name: A: Threshold-triggered escalation plus stronger shared host-independence predicate
pros: Keeps normal one-round REVIEW for clean stories
Automatically escalates stories with first-round quality risk
Reuses and strengthens the existing decision-doc quorum model
Provides one shared independence predicate for future gates
cons: Requires new evaluator and artifact work in a later implementation story
Requires careful stale-material handling so verdicts cannot be reused after changes

options.name: B: Force every story through 3 rounds x 2 hosts
cons: High latency and cost for trivial stories
Likely to create review fatigue and rubber-stamp behavior
Does not directly fix the existing host independence spoof gap

options.name: C: Keep 3x2 only for decision docs
cons: Fails the user-requested rule for all development
Misses risky implementation stories whose first review round exposes multiple verified problems
Leaves no escalation artifact for non-doc stories

chosen: A: Threshold-triggered escalation plus stronger shared host-independence predicate
rationale: Choose threshold-triggered escalation because it satisfies the explicit all-development rule while keeping normal development usable. The implementation plan must first strengthen host independence, then add a reusable escalation evaluator and DONE gate consumption path.

preMortem.scenario: Escalation can be spoofed by changing hostId strings while the same host, session, or key submits all passes.
preMortem.trigger: The evaluator counts display hostId only and ignores sessionId or keyId.
preMortem.mitigation: Persist hostId, provider, sessionId, keyId, and signed identity facts in host_verdict process events, then count independent host groups through one shared predicate.

preMortem.scenario: Every story becomes slow because 3x2 is applied unconditionally.
preMortem.trigger: Implementation treats the policy as global always-on instead of first-round threshold-triggered.
preMortem.consequence: Review fatigue increases and ordinary fixes become expensive.
preMortem.mitigation: Default to normal REVIEW; trigger escalation only for decision-doc changes or first REVIEW round verified finding count >= 2, with optional critical finding policy explicitly documented.

preMortem.scenario: A story fixes first-round findings and later reuses stale 3x2 verdicts after material changes.
preMortem.trigger: Host verdicts are not bound to final HEAD, material, and validation digest.
preMortem.consequence: DONE can pass with reviews over old material.
preMortem.mitigation: Bind every counted verdict to current material digest and validation digest; stale digest mismatch must fail closed.

preMortem.scenario: The new rule is documented but not enforced in lifecycle gates.
preMortem.trigger: Only AGENTS, README, or prompt text changes are made.
preMortem.consequence: Agents may skip escalation and still enter DONE.
preMortem.mitigation: Add process fact registry entries, CLI status command, evaluator tests, and DONE gate failure reasons as mandatory implementation acceptance criteria.
